_comment: Tile -> pixel transform per map image. The art is not a plain render of the
ROM map: DarkmoonEX's maps are drawn by hand and composited, so parts of a
floor can sit at unrelated offsets and iceB3 carries two floors side by side.
'rows' and 'cols' bound a region by ROM tile, inclusive; the first matching
region wins and a region with no bounds matches everything.
x = offset_x + col*tile_px + tile_px/2, and PopTracker centres the marker on
that point -- so offset_x/offset_y locate the top-left of ROM tile (0,0) in
the image, NOT the top-left of any drawn sprite. Getting that wrong is what
put the first cut of this file a sprite-corner up and to the left on every
marker, and made iceB3 look like it needed two regions when it needs one.
Each offset here was solved from the centroid of the drawn chest sprites
(the chest body is exactly RGB(200,76,12)) against the ROM tile coordinates,
then checked on the overlay. See tools/overlay_preview.py.
tofrChaos was solved a different way on 2026-09-05, because a floor the
vanilla game gives no chest offers no centroid to solve from -- the seven
chests there are laid by ShortToFR, and the hand art predates them. The
room's own extent works instead: every ToFR map lays its room from ROM tile
(0,0), and the drawn room is the same size as the ROM room, so the offset is
the far content edge minus the room's pixel width plus one. That rule
reproduces tofr3F (32,22), tofrFire (10,9) and tofrAir (12,12) exactly,
which is why it is trusted here; the near edge does NOT reproduce tofrAir,
whose art carries three rows of something above the room.
Do not use edge energy to find the grid phase. It was tried and it does not
reproduce any of the three known offsets -- the strongest edges in hand-drawn
art are inside the tiles, not on their boundaries.
tofrChaos was then confirmed twice over: the implied 16px grid lines up with
the drawn tile boundaries across the landmark area, and the one teal object
in the room centres at (259,132), which under (13,13) is col 14.88 row 6.94
-- ROM tile (15,7), the only special tile in that column (0x3B, b1 0xBF).
Note (15,7), not (15,5): the ToFR handoff named the wrong row.
tofr1F, tofrEarth and tofrWater were solved on 2026-09-06 and each entry
carries the reading it was solved from. The method that reached the two
interior floors is a landmark and not a heuristic: every ToFR floor but 1F,
2F and Chaos carries exactly one fixed-formation battle tile -- the fiend --
at the same ROM coordinates on all five cartridges measured here, vanilla
included, and DarkmoonEX draws a yellow boss plate on it. Read the plate's
blob (RGB(242,201,11)), read the tile off the cartridge with
render_maps.map_trap_marks, and the offset is the difference.
It reproduces tofrFire (10,9) and tofrAir (12,12) to within a pixel in x and
exactly in y. On tofr3F it lands 4 px high -- that art draws its plate 4 px
above the tile centre, which is an idiosyncrasy of the one map rather than a
wrong entry: the two drawn chest sprites there sit at the same (-2,-3.5) from
their tile centres that they do on tofrFire and tofrAir, so 22 is right and
the plate is high. Read that as the method's error bar. Never take a plate as
the only evidence for a y.
Why the room-extent rule did not answer these three. On tofr1F it proposes
(54,39), and the overlay says WRONG -- the grid lines up nowhere. The cause
is room_tiles(): it calls the most common tile the void, and tofr1F is the
one Temple floor drawn with the outdoors around it, so the commonest tile is
grass and the box it returns is the temple rather than the drawn area. Ask
the same question about the temple instead and it answers: the temple spans
42x37 ROM tiles and the art's non-grass box is 673x592, so y is 20 on both
edges and x is 27 or 28. On tofrWater it proposes (31,22), and 31 is the Map
Key panel rather than the room -- exclude the rows the panel occupies and the
room measures exactly 496 px from x 22, which is what the boss plate says
too. On tofrEarth it proposes (13,18), the plate agrees, and that one was
right all along.
One more thing the overlay makes obvious: images/maps/*.png are DarkmoonEX's
annotated maps, carrying a title bar, a Map Key and his own drawn route. The
content box therefore includes furniture that is not the room, which is why
the far edge is the anchor and the near edge is not.
Three ways of confirming an offset without a person looking were tried on
2026-09-05 and all three failed. Do not spend the afternoon on a fourth
without reading these first:
- edge energy over the whole image: dominated by the title bar and the
frame, and it ranks no known offset first.
- edge energy restricted to the room: still ranks the true phase only 2nd
to 5th of 16 on the four floors whose offset is known.
- saturated-sprite centroids against tile centres: the clustering splits
sprites across cells, and tofrFire, which is correct, scores worse than
proposals that are wrong.
The reason is the same each time: hand-drawn tiles carry more contrast
inside them than at their edges. The overlay and a person is the test.
A fourth was tried and failed differently, and is the most tempting of the
lot: correlating the ROM's wall/floor mask against the art's per-tile
brightness. The correlation is genuinely high -- 0.70 to 0.83 -- and its peak
is 3 to 5 pixels away from the known answer on all four floors that have one.
It finds the room, not the grid.
A fifth, tried 2026-09-06 and worth naming because it looks like the
landmark method and is not: scoring an offset by how often the art agrees
with the cartridge about which tiles are void, sampled at every tile centre.
It scores 0.97 to 1.00 on offsets that are demonstrably wrong -- a mostly
empty mask agrees with itself at many phases -- and recovers none of the five
known offsets. A high score over a uniform region says nothing.
Do not try to solve tofr1F, tofrEarth or tofrWater from chest sprites. The
art draws four chests on tofr1F and none on the other two, and chest_tiles()
puts NO chest tile on any of the three -- on a Long cartridge only tofr3F has
any, at (17,15) and (23,15), which is exactly what its committed offset
implies and is a good check that the transform above is right. Whatever
tofr1F's drawn chests depict, the cartridge does not agree, so they cannot
anchor an offset.

_derived_from.note: Lich (map object $1B), placed at 79,347 in SunflashRune/FFR_AP_autotracking@upstream/Sun. offset_x agrees exactly with earthB4's, which was solved independently from chest sprites.

_solved_from.how: the temple outline, cross-checked against the four corner stair glyphs
_solved_from.note: The one Temple floor with no fiend to anchor on. The ROM map's own grass is the void, so the temple spans ROM cols 0-41 and rows 0-36 (42x37 tiles = 672x592 px) and the art's non-grass box is x 27-699, y 20-611. The y span is 592 exactly and both edges agree on 20. The x span is 673, one pixel wider than the grid, so the near edge gives 27 and the far edge 28; the four cyan stair glyphs imply 27.0 at ROM (1,1), 28.5 at (40,1), 26.0 at (1,35) and 28.5 at (40,35) -- the art runs about 1.5 px wide across its width, and no single offset is exact at both ends. They straddle the answer rather than settling it, which is why the near edge decides and the glyphs only have to agree within 2 px. 27 is the near-edge answer and the chest copies Mid lays here, 253 at (16,16) and 254 at (24,16), sit mid-map where the stretch is smallest.

_solved_from.how: Lich's battle tile, cross-checked against the room extent
_solved_from.note: The drawn boss badge (the yellow LI plate, RGB(242,201,11)) centres at (596.5,506.0) and the map's one fixed-formation tile is ROM (36,30) on every cartridge measured, vanilla included, which gives (12.5,18.0). The room's own extent gives (13,18) on both edges -- 39x34 tiles against a 624x544 art box -- so two independent readings agree.

_solved_from.how: Kraken's battle tile, cross-checked against the room extent below the Map Key
_solved_from.note: The badge centres at (414.5,478.0) against ROM (24,28), which gives (22.5,22.0). The room measures exactly 496 px, x 22-517, once the rows carrying the Map Key panel are excluded -- 31 tiles, both edges hard. Taking the whole image instead puts the far edge at 526 and proposes offset_x 31, which is the Map Key and not the room: at 31 the marker box cuts the badge in half and the implied grid bisects every wall block.

_uncalibrated.sky5F: sky5F.png is not 16 px per tile -- map 51's content is 15x56 tiles, which at 16 px would be 896 tall against the image's 414. Tiamat's pixel upstream/Sun cannot be reproduced by a single 16 px region, so no entry is guessed here.
_uncalibrated.bahamut: bahamut.png is one image for two ROM maps, 17 and 39 stacked. Bahamut himself is on 39. A single region cannot describe it; the multi-region form (see cardia) can, but wants a second correspondence on map 17 to pin down.
